verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go to Pharaoh and tell him, 'This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they can worship me.
If you refuse to let them go and keep holding on to them,
the hand of the LORD will bring a terrible disease on your animals in the fields: on your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, sheep, and goats.
But the LORD will treat the animals of Israel differently from the animals of Egypt. Not one animal that belongs to the people of Israel will die.'"
The LORD set a time and said, "Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land."
And the next day the LORD did it. All the animals of the Egyptians died, but not one animal of the people of Israel died.
Pharaoh sent people to look, and they found that not even one of the animals of the Israelites had died. But Pharaoh's heart was still stubborn, and he would not let the people go.
Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Take handfuls of soot from a furnace, and let Moses throw it into the air in front of Pharaoh.
It will become fine dust over the whole land of Egypt. It will cause boils to break out into open sores on people and animals all over Egypt."
So they took soot from a furnace and stood in front of Pharaoh. Moses threw it into the air, and boils broke out into open sores on people and animals.
The magicians could not stand in front of Moses because of the boils, because the boils were on the magicians and on all the Egyptians.
But the LORD made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, and he would not listen to Moses and Aaron, just as the LORD had told Moses.

Then the LORD said to Moses, "Get up early in the morning, stand in front of Pharaoh, and tell him, 'This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go, so that they can worship me.
This time I will send all my plagues against you, against your officials, and against your people, so that you will know that there is no one like me in all the earth.
By now I could have reached out my hand and struck you and your people with a disease that would have wiped you off the earth.
But I have let you live for this reason: to show you my power, and so that my name will be made known in all the earth.
You still set yourself up against my people and will not let them go.
So at this time tomorrow I will send the worst hailstorm that has ever fallen on Egypt, from the day it became a nation until now.

So give an order now to bring your animals and everything you have in the fields into shelter. The hail will fall on every person and animal that is left out in the field and not brought inside, and they will die.'"
Some of Pharaoh's officials feared the word of the LORD. They hurried to bring their slaves and their animals inside.
But those who ignored the word of the LORD left their slaves and their animals in the field.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the sky, so that hail will fall all over Egypt, on people and animals, and on every plant growing in the fields of Egypt."
When Moses stretched out his staff toward the sky, the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning flashed down to the ground. So the LORD made hail fall on the land of Egypt.
The hail fell, and lightning flashed back and forth among the hail. It was the worst storm in all the land of Egypt since it had become a nation.
All over Egypt the hail struck everything in the fields, both people and animals. It beat down every plant in the fields and broke every tree.
The only place where there was no hail was the land of Goshen, where the people of Israel lived.
Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron. He said to them, "This time I have sinned. The LORD is right, and I and my people are wrong.
Pray to the LORD, because we have had enough of this thunder and hail. I will let you go. You do not have to stay any longer."

Moses answered him, "When I have gone out of the city, I will lift up my hands in prayer to the LORD. The thunder will stop, and there will be no more hail, so that you will know that the earth belongs to the LORD.
But I know that you and your officials still do not fear the LORD God."
The flax and the barley were destroyed, because the barley had formed its heads and the flax was in flower.
But the wheat and the spelt were not destroyed, because they ripen later.
Then Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He lifted up his hands to the LORD. The thunder and the hail stopped, and the rain no longer poured down on the land.
When Pharaoh saw that the rain, the hail, and the thunder had stopped, he sinned again. He and his officials made their hearts stubborn.
So Pharaoh's heart was stubborn, and he would not let the people of Israel go, just as the LORD had said through Moses.
